text:
maria: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands re: GPUs and holiday capacity. A couple of customers asked whether well guarantee H100 capacity or rely on fallbacks. Can we summarise the plan here?

jamal: tl;dr: we do not plan to buy blanket short-term reserved racks for holidays. We'll use a hybrid approach: preemptible burst pools + targeted reserved top-ups for enterprise SLAs. Fallbacks to A100/Q8 model variants for non-critical traffic.

devon: timeline for reserved top-ups? procurement ETA?

jamal: procurement for additional H100 inventory slipped ~2-3 weeks due to vendor queue. That pushed the earliest regional delivery into late next month. So holiday week = use orchestration + cross-region routing.

cto-matt: is cross-region routing acceptable for enterprise with data-residency needs?

jamal: short answer: no for strict residency customers. For those we will offer paid reserved top-ups and advise early commit. Private deployments unaffected. We'll work with legal/customer-success on exceptions.

sara: ops question: what exactly will the autoscaler do if preemptibles vanish mid-spike? Need to update oncall runbooks.

jamal: autoscaler fallback steps: 1) try local preemptible pool; 2) after preemptible_unavail_secs (default 75s) start draining traffic to reserved pool if allowed by customer tier; 3) if no reserved, route to smaller model variants (vsmall/vbase) and mark request with degraded_quality tag. We also have circuit-breaker thresholds to limit blast radius.

maria: Can we get the concrete knobs so CS/ops can read them?

jamal: pasted canary/autoscaler snippet below for ops to copy:

```
# burst canary & autoscaler (excerpt)
canary: 0.12
canary_window: 25m
preemptible_unavail_secs: 75
reserved_fallback_enabled: true
model_variant_fallback_order: ["vbase", "vsmall"]
autoscaler_triggers: ["queue_length", "gpu_util_pct", "p95_latency"]
scale_up_step: 2
scale_down_step: 1
cooldown_up: 15s
cooldown_down: 120s
failure_inject: {"preemptible_kill_pct": 40, "after_secs": 60}
```

deploy-bot: canary_schedule: burst-orch-canary scheduled 2028-06-04T09:00:00Z by jamal.

devon: Nice. I'll add a synthetic scenario to the canary job that simulates a 40% preemptible termination after 60s. Should we also test cross-region reroute latency?

jamal: yes, add a cross-region latency probe for eu-west <-> apac paths. We need SLOs for cross-region options documented in the console.

sara: I'll own the runbook updates and customer comms drafts. Creating ticket now.

sara: created INFRA-4902 with runbook checklist + comms draft.

maria: Can we also make a short explainer for sales so they can advise enterprise customers about reserved top-ups and pricing?

cto-matt: +1. Sales should get a one-pager before the holiday window. finance needs an estimate of incremental reserved spend if we keep top-ups.

jamal: i'll produce a one-pager and an estimated cost delta for a 1-week reserved top-up scenario per region. Will post in #all-hands-followups.

maria: thanks. one more ask  any change needed in client SDKs?

jamal: no client-side changes for default behavior. If customers want to opt into reserved-only routing or strict latency SLO enforcement we'll expose server-side flags in the console and via the admin API.

devon: logistic note: we should add an alert that fires if preemptible_pool_util drops > 30% in under 2m during the canary window. Ops can then triage quickly.

jamal: agree. i'll add that alert to the canary runbook.

maria: great. I'll coordinate with CS on messaging and with sales on the one-pager. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:

sara: ping me if you want to review the runbook before I merge.

devon: will watch the canary and post results.

maria: closing the loop here.
